items.title: George "Pops" Foster Interview, 1957-04-21
items.q: I worked on the boat with Dewey Jackson.

ctx.x: So you got to know where all those rocks are. Yeah. How long were you with Faith Merrill?

From about, 1918 afternoon till about around 19. 19, 19, 19, I didn't work with Faith No More on the boat. But I worked on the boat and I went back on the boat with, uh- I worked on the boat with Dewey Jackson. I worked on the boat with Eddie Allen. I worked on the boat with, uh, Charlotte Craig. I worked on the island Queen too, or the Cincinnati. And the captain got all sorted with us. Man, we had the people screaming. And he said, Jesus Christ, you fell in a bunch of sticks. They got us screaming over there.…

items.title: George "Pops" Foster Interview, 1958-08-24
items.q: Yeah, I was on the Charlie Crust with Dewey Jackson. We made records so safe then

ctx.x: Yeah, that's that picture where you were playing tuba.

Then I played for the Elves Parade. I was at a convention in Chicago. And I went on to Chicago. Passed through St. Louis, told Dewey I'd be back. That's when Johnny wanted me to stay with him. With all them kids. See? I joined the Drew Jackson band and stayed with the Drew Jackson band then from September 28th until February 29th. I went to the Louis Russell band. I stayed with Louis Russell. That fills that. I stayed with Louis Russell until 1940. That's when Joe fired the whole band for the Chief of Band. He…
I was going to ask about your very first records. Were you on an old record that Fate Marable made with Sidney Dez Bean and Amos White? No.
